quandoUsar: Toolbar whose width changes (resizable panels, narrow columns, small screens) and that has more actions than fit.
When all actions must stay reachable: the ones that do not fit go into the “more” menu, starting with the last ones in the list.
quandoEvitar: Use `button-group` when there are a few related actions that always fit.
Use `dropdown-menu` when secondary actions can live in a menu from the start.
Use `toggle-group` for formatting toggles that always fit and do not need a menu.

teclado.acao: Move focus between the visible actions and the “more” button, wrapping around at the ends and skipping disabled ones.
Move focus to the first or last stop of the bar.
The bar has a single Tab stop; the arrow keys do the rest.
Activate the focused action or open the “more” menu.
In the “more” menu, move between items; `↓` on the button also opens the menu.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the “more” button.

acessibilidade: The bar is a `role="toolbar"` with an `aria-label` coming from `label` and roving tabindex; actions with `pressed` expose `aria-pressed`.
The “more” button receives `moreLabel` with the count in the `aria-label`, and in the menu an active action gets a dot with the text “On” for screen readers.
The measuring row, with copies of all the actions, is `aria-hidden` and `inert`.
movimento: Actions that stop fitting shrink to 80% and fade, and the ones that return do the reverse; the “more” button slides to its new position on a layout spring.
The number on the “more” button rolls vertically when the count changes, and the menu opens with the items in a 28 ms cascade.
With “reduce motion” on, entries, exits, and shifts happen instantly and the menu animations are removed.
responsivo: The width that counts is the component's own, which takes 100% of its parent: it measures all the actions in a hidden row and shows as many as fit, never wrapping to a new line.
When no action fits, only the “more” button remains, with all of them inside the menu.
desempenho: A `ResizeObserver` watches the root and the measuring row and recomputes on every change of width, label, or font; each action is rendered twice because of that copy.
notasIA: Import the named component `OverflowActions`; the default export is the preview of an editor with a resize handle.
Order `actions` by priority, because the last ones go to the menu first, and give the container a real width (in flex, `min-width: 0`).
`pressed` is controlled by you: keep the state and toggle it in `onSelect` or `onAction(id)`; `onOverflowChange(ids)` reports which actions are in the menu.
